digest.component_or_area: bridge surface / library and MCP integration
propositions: New noun-based bridge operations (preview, sync, status, pause, resume, check_access) must be exported as typed public library functions and registered as MCP tools with explicit options and no mode vocabulary.
Legacy rebar.reconcile(mode=...) and bridge_fsck must remain callable with unchanged signatures, defaults, return types, exception behavior, and published schemas for backward compatibility.
Library and MCP adapters must reuse the shared run_pass() / _Disposition classification seam instead of duplicating route/exit-code logic or invoking the CLI.
mcp.allow_jira_sync must gate every mutating route (bridge_sync, bridge_pause, bridge_resume, mutating reconcile modes) while permitting reads (preview, status, fsck, access-check).
Each new MCP tool must publish an outputSchema; old compatibility schemas must remain valid after new tool registration.

Legacy reconcile modes must map consistently to new bridge operations (dry-run/reconcile-check → preview with cap 0, bootstrap-strict → sync with max-changes 10, bootstrap-throttle → sync with max-changes 100, live → uncapped sync) via shared mode policy rather than copied tables.
